original_question: For a regular polynomial sequence (f_n), find simple formulas for the Hausdorff dimension of the measure μ_{J(f_n)} supported on the generalized Julia set J(f_n). Here the Hausdorff dimension of a unit Borel measure μ is defined by dim(μ)=inf{HD(K): μ(K)=1}.
target_in_paper: Problem 11 in Section 4 (“Hausdorff measures”): “Is it possible to find simple formulas for dim(μ_{J(f_n)}) where (f_n) is a regular polynomial sequence?” ([drna.padovauniversitypress.it](https://drna.padovauniversitypress.it/system/files/papers/AlpanGoncharov_DRNA2017.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the exact open problem’s subject matter: regular polynomial sequences, the generalized Julia set J(f_n), the measure-dimension functional dim(μ)=inf{HD(K): μ(K)=1}, and the search for simple formulas. Those are exactly the ingredients used immediately before and in Problem 11. ([drna.padovauniversitypress.it](https://drna.padovauniversitypress.it/system/files/papers/AlpanGoncharov_DRNA2017.pdf))
missing_details: The paper’s measure is not an arbitrary unit Borel measure merely supported on J(f_n); it is the equilibrium measure μ_{J(f_n)} of the compact set J(f_n). The notation μ_K for equilibrium measure is introduced earlier, and Section 1.2 states that J(f_n) is a regular compact set of positive capacity for regular polynomial sequences. ([drna.padovauniversitypress.it](https://drna.padovauniversitypress.it/system/files/papers/AlpanGoncharov_DRNA2017.pdf))

The ambient space is the complex plane C, and J(f_n) is the Julia set of a non-autonomous sequence of rational/polynomial maps, not the Julia set of a single autonomous polynomial unless all f_n are equal. ([drna.padovauniversitypress.it](https://drna.padovauniversitypress.it/system/files/papers/AlpanGoncharov_DRNA2017.pdf))

To be stand-alone, the question should define F_n=f_n∘f_{n-1}∘⋯∘f_1 and say that J(f_n) is the complement in C of the Fatou set of the family (F_n). ([drna.padovauniversitypress.it](https://drna.padovauniversitypress.it/system/files/papers/AlpanGoncharov_DRNA2017.pdf))

The phrase “regular polynomial sequence” must be spelled out: each f_n(z)=∑_{j=0}^{d_n} a_{n,j} z^j with d_n≥2 and a_{n,d_n}≠0, and there exist constants A_1,A_2,A_3>0 such that for every n, |a_{n,d_n}|≥A_1, |a_{n,j}|≤A_2|a_{n,d_n}| for 0≤j≤d_n−1, and log|a_{n,d_n}|≤A_3 d_n. ([drna.padovauniversitypress.it](https://drna.padovauniversitypress.it/system/files/papers/AlpanGoncharov_DRNA2017.pdf))

The paper asks an existence-style open problem—“Is it possible to find simple formulas ...?”—rather than directly asserting that one should now derive such formulas. Matching that modality keeps the question faithful to the paper. ([drna.padovauniversitypress.it](https://drna.padovauniversitypress.it/system/files/papers/AlpanGoncharov_DRNA2017.pdf))

If the question is to be fully self-contained, it should explicitly identify HD as Hausdorff dimension of sets and dim(μ) as the infimum of HD(E) over full μ-measure sets E⊂C, exactly as stated in Section 4. ([drna.padovauniversitypress.it](https://drna.padovauniversitypress.it/system/files/papers/AlpanGoncharov_DRNA2017.pdf))
refined_question: Let (f_n)_{n≥1} be a regular polynomial sequence in C in the sense that each f_n(z)=∑_{j=0}^{d_n} a_{n,j} z^j has d_n≥2 and a_{n,d_n}≠0, and there exist constants A_1,A_2,A_3>0 such that for every n, |a_{n,d_n}|≥A_1, |a_{n,j}|≤A_2|a_{n,d_n}| for 0≤j≤d_n−1, and log|a_{n,d_n}|≤A_3 d_n. Write F_n=f_n∘f_{n-1}∘⋯∘f_1, let J(f_n) denote the Julia set of the non-autonomous sequence (f_n), and let μ_{J(f_n)} be the equilibrium measure of the regular compact set J(f_n). Is it possible to find simple formulas for dim(μ_{J(f_n)}), where dim(μ):=inf{HD(E): μ(E)=1}? ([drna.padovauniversitypress.it](https://drna.padovauniversitypress.it/system/files/papers/AlpanGoncharov_DRNA2017.pdf))
justification: The draft is targeting Problem 11 almost verbatim. The only paper-faithful sharpening needed is to restore the precise Section 1.2 definition of “regular polynomial sequence,” to define J(f_n) via the non-autonomous iterates F_n, and to make explicit that μ_{J(f_n)} is the equilibrium measure on J(f_n), whose existence is justified because Section 1.2 states that J(f_n) is a regular compact set with positive capacity. The measure-dimension definition in your draft already matches the paragraph immediately preceding Problem 11. ([drna.padovauniversitypress.it](https://drna.padovauniversitypress.it/system/files/papers/AlpanGoncharov_DRNA2017.pdf))
